header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Time: 14:30 - 15:16 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Anika Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Meridian Labs, ML Platform), Priya Anand (Meridian Labs, SRE), Amir Ben-David (Meridian Labs, CTO)
Meeting purpose: Weekly POC check-in for inference latency tuning (TTFT, streaming, seq len, kernel routing)
summary: Mid-pilot sync to review last 72h of experiment data: TTFT degradation at Seq>512, streaming tradeoffs, and kernel routing mismatches. Redwood presented trimmed kernel perf and a proposed canary: route 10% traffic to cuBLAS-quantized binary vs Triton-optimized path. Customer asked for a steady-state 1-hour run at seq=1024 and to validate KV cache effectiveness for repeated prefixes. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share perf CSV and pricing worksheet; Meridian to run steady-state test and validate VPC egress. Plan for kernel fallback A/B next week.
topics: TTFT regressions at longer sequence lengths
kernel selection: Triton vs cuBLAS vs fbgemm (notes/misreads)
routing policy for Dedicated vs Hosted
transcript:
[00:00] Lena (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, uh, quick roll call?
[00:07] Jordan: Jordan here, Priya and Amir on my side.
[00:10] Priya: Yep, Priya present.
[00:12] Marco (SE): Marco from Redwood, Anika on mute.
[00:15] Amir: Amir, CTO.
[00:18] Lena: Great, goal today — go through the last 72 hours of runs, the TTFT spikes at longer sequences, and then discuss kernel routing canary. Should be ~45 minutes.
[00:30] Marco: Quick note, we uploaded the trimmed kernel perf CSV — it's in the shared drive link in the calendar invite, the file name starts with "meridian-kernel-trim-20260406.csv". It's the one where we compared Triton tuned kernels, cuBLAS quant path, and the FBGEMM-ish quantization on the CPU fallback.
[00:45] Jordan: I saw that, thanks. Wanted to clarify — when you say TTFT spike at seq 768, is that cold-start or steady-state?
[00:55] Marco: Good q. The dataset has both cold and warm. The spike is mostly warm-state — we saw p50 stable but p95 jumps when KV cache miss rate increased above ~18%. So it's not pure cold-start.
[01:10] Priya: We did see periodic miss bursts — our workload has a lot of varying prefixes so K V cash... uh I mean KV cache effectiveness drops.
[01:20] Anika (SE): Yeah, also worth noting the streaming path adds ~12-18ms overhead on the server side in our config because of chunk assembly and TLS framing. It's still better for perceived latency on the client, but TTFT measured at first-token emission can be worse if chunking waits for small buffers.
[01:40] Amir: So the tradeoff is perceived streaming vs measured first token. For our product, early partial token is better.
[01:48] Lena: Right, product asks for perceived latency, but we're tracking TTFT as a SLO. We should align on which metric Meridian prioritizes.
[01:58] Jordan: Perceived, but we need p95 under 300ms for triage flows.
[02:05] Marco: Understood. In the CSV, the Triton optimized path at seq=256 p95 was ~210ms, but at seq=1024 it creeped to ~420ms under our test load. The cuBLAS-quant path held better on GPU memory pressure but had tokenization variance.
[02:30] Priya: Can you explain the memory pressure bit — are you evicting KV cache aggressively?
[02:36] Marco: We simulated slightly lower batch buffer and that forced more KV chunk evictions which increased memory churn; the runtime then fell back to a slower kernel for larger attention windows. Also there was a kernel scheduling decision that favored a spatially optimized kernel that didn't handle the long tail as well.
[02:58] Jordan: Is that the kernel selector you mentioned last time — the one that picks based on seq length distribution?
[03:03] Anika: Yup, it's the runtime heuristic. It uses historic sequence histograms and tries to pick the fastest kernel; but when distribution shifts, there's a misroute. We're proposing adding a short windowed predictor to smooth decisions.
[03:18] Amir: What's the risk of switching kernel mid-flight?
[03:21] Marco: No correctness issue, only perf jitter. The KV cache keys remain compatible. But there could be TensorRT/Triton SLO tradeoff if we change execution engine real-time — small transient latency.
[03:36] Priya: For VPC/Private, we also need to ensure we don't hit egress throttles during the experiments.
[03:43] Lena: Good call — Priya, you'll check with infra team and confirm egress policy?
[03:47] Priya: Yup, will confirm and share by Friday.
[03:51] Jordan: Back to streaming — you mentioned chunk assembly cost, is that mostly on the client or server?
[03:58] Marco: Server-side assembly and TLS framing plus the server waiting for a minimal chunk size. We can tune minimal chunk size which reduces server-side cost but increases first-byte jitter for longer outputs.
[04:15] Jordan: Is there an opt to send a tiny first chunk (like 1 token) ASAP then rest as larger chunks?
[04:20] Anika: Yes, the runtime supports low-latency first-chunk then bigger payloads. There's a slight extra CPU tax but for most of your flows it's worth it.
[04:30] Amir: You recommended a canary for kernel routing?
[04:33] Marco: Proposed canary: route 10% of traffic for a fixed route to cuBLAS quantized kernels with aggressive KV persistence; compare p95 and error rates for 24 hours. If stable, bump to 30% then 50%.
[04:48] Lena: We'll also instrument a short histogram of seq lengths to feed the selector's predictor; that'll help avoid misroutes.
[04:56] Jordan: For storage, where do we push the detailed logs? We prefer S3 with lifecycle.
[04:59] Marco: S3 link is in the perf spreadsheet notes. We'll add a separate folder for the canary logs.
[05:07] Priya: One more question on quant — does cuBLAS quant change output distribution? We saw subtle token probability shifts in earlier runs.
[05:15] Anika: There's small distribution shift, yes. Our quality evals flagged a 0.3% drop on exact-match for a narrow eval set. We can do a side-by-side eval run focusing on your core prompts.
[05:28] Amir: That's risky for the feature. We need to validate with real prompt set before we roll.
[05:33] Lena: Agreed — next step: Redwood will run offline quality eval with Meridian prompt set against cuBLAS quant path and Triton baseline.
[05:43] Jordan: We'll share a trimmed prompt set — about 200 prompts — privacy reviewed.
[05:47] Jordan: Also, can we get a price delta estimate if we go Dedicated with reserved capacity?
[05:52] Lena: Yes — sending Dedicated worksheet and a few capacity scenarios. You'll see estimated unit token costs with our suggested batching and quant combos.
[05:58] Priya: On batching — is dynamic batching enabled for streaming?
[06:02] Marco: Streaming and batching are orthogonal in our runtime; we can do intra-step batching of small chunks, but it requires careful latency knobs. For your SLOs, we suggested batching target = 8 with max latency 80ms. That was used in the CSV runs.
[06:20] Amir: How deterministic are the perf numbers? We saw variance between runs.
[06:24] Marco: We recommend steady-state 1-hour tests at target QPS; the numbers in the CSV were 10-minute windows. The 1-hour tends to reduce variance and show evictions/slowdowns.
[06:36] Jordan: We'll run a 1-hour at seq=1024 per Marco's suggestion. Anything else for the test?
[06:41] Marco: Capture KV hit/miss, GPU mem pressure, and the runtime kernel logs. We'll provide a tracer snippet.
[06:47] Anika: Also include a short warmup period of 10 minutes so KV warms. Keep the first 10 minutes separate for analysis.
[06:54] Jordan: Good.
[06:56] Lena: Let's pivot to a quick review of the perf CSV — Marco?
[07:01] Marco: Slide through: seq=256 shows Triton p95 210ms, cuBLAS-quant p95 195ms; seq=512 Triton 290ms, cuBLAS 270ms; seq=1024 Triton 420ms, cuBLAS 360ms but at higher variance. The CPU fallback (FBGEMM-like) did worse for large seq but held up for tiny batches.
[07:30] Amir: The delta at 1024 seems compelling but variance is concerning. How often did mem pressure cause fallback?
[07:36] Marco: In the runs with heavy burstiness, fallback events were ~3 per 10k requests. In steady-state long-run they were lower.
[07:46] Priya: What triggers the fallback exactly? Kernel OOM or scheduling decision?
[07:50] Marco: Mostly memory fragmentation leading to an inability to bind a bigger attention buffer; then scheduler picks a less memory-heavy kernel.
[07:59] Anika: We can pin a memory headroom param to reduce fragmentation but it costs throughput.
[08:06] Jordan: Can that headroom be tuned per route? We have routes with predictable seq distribution.
[08:10] Marco: Yes, route-level config supports memory headroom plus cache sizing. We can recommend values for your three main routes.
[08:18] Lena: Jordan, can you share your route list and rough seq distribution after the call? That'll let Marco propose config.
[08:23] Jordan: Yep, will share.
[08:25] Marco: Quick note: there was a small mislabel in the CSV where a column read "fb-gemm" but it was actually a CPU quant shim; ignore that label, we corrected it in the notes.
[08:37] Priya: Ha, ok. The transcripts sometimes have that too.
[08:40] Lena: Back to streaming knobs — if we send a tiny first chunk and then bulk, do we lose any token-level caching?
[08:47] Anika: No, KV/prefix caching unaffected. It's purely chunking at the transport layer.
[08:52] Amir: Are we comfortable with pushing a 10% cuBLAS route during business hours?
[08:57] Marco: Yes, 10% should be safe. We'll monitor error budgets and auto-roll back on any spike.
[09:03] Jordan: How long should the canary run to be meaningful?
[09:06] Marco: 24-48 hours; 24 hours will catch diurnal patterns but 48 gives more confidence.
[09:11] Priya: We'll start with 24 and extend if stable.
[09:14] Lena: Perfect. On the instrumentation side, we'll add a few counters: kernel_selected, kv_hit, kv_miss, mem_pressure_flag, and ttft_ms. We'll push Grafana dashboard links after the call.
[09:26] Jordan: Cool. Couple nitpicks — tokenization variance with cuBLAS quant means our downstream detokenizer had minor diffs which matter for our metrics. Can you include a detokenizer-aware comparison?
[09:38] Anika: Yes, we'll do detokenizer-normalized scoring.
[09:42] Amir: Anything else re security/compliance? We need to ensure logs in S3 are encrypted and access controlled.
[09:48] Lena: We will by default enable SSE-KMS and a bucket policy; Priya verify with infra.
[09:54] Priya: Will confirm and reply in CRM thread.
[09:58] Marco: One more perf note — when sequence distribution is bimodal it confuses the kernel selector. The predictor fix would average histograms over the last N minutes instead of relying on immediate window. That helps stability.
[10:14] Jordan: Sounds good. Any estimate for effort to implement predictor?
[10:18] Marco: Small change — 1-2 engineer days to add config and 3-4 days to validate in canary. We can prioritize it after the canary results.
[10:28] Lena: Ok. Let's capture immediate next steps and owners — Jordan will run the 1-hour seq=1024 steady-state test, Priya to confirm egress/keys, Marco/Anika to upload corrected perf CSV and tracer snippet, Lena to send pricing/worksheet.
[10:45] Jordan: I'll likely run test Wednesday afternoon.
[10:48] Lena: Good. Any blockers on Redwood side?
[10:51] Marco: None — we'll support the S3 ingestion and provide the tracer.
[10:55] Amir: Quick question about cost — if we choose Dedicated reserved capacity, how quickly can you provision?
[11:01] Lena: For reserved pools, typically 2-3 weeks for capacity carveouts, but we can do an interim Dedicated burst in 48-72 hours for pilot scale.
[11:12] Amir: Ok that works.
[11:15] Priya: Regarding logs retention, we'll want 90 days for pilot. Possible?
[11:19] Lena: Yes, retention configurable; will add note in worksheet.
[11:23] Marco: Also — we spotted a tiny request routing bug in the older agent that mis-attributed some requests to the wrong route when route names had similar prefixes; we've patched it in the canary branch. If you use route names with unique prefixes you'll be fine.
[11:38] Jordan: Noted. We'll avoid similar prefixes.
[11:41] Anika: Ok quick timeline proposal: Today — action items captured. 4/9 — Redwood uploads perf and pricing; 4/13 — Meridian runs 1-hour test; 4/14 — run kernel A/B canary if results look good.
[11:57] Amir: Works for me.
[12:00] Lena: Any final questions?
[12:02] Priya: One small ask — can you include a note on how rollback is automated on error budget exceed?
[12:09] Marco: Yes we'll include rollback thresholds and the automation snippet in the Runbook.
[12:14] Jordan: Thanks, this was helpful.
[12:16] Lena: Great — I'll send the recap and worksheet. We'll reconvene same time next week unless we need an earlier check-in.
[12:22] Marco: Thanks all.
[12:25] Amir: Thanks, bye.
[12:27] [call ended]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings — "K V cash" for KV cache, "fb-gemm" label typo noted above. Natural pauses and crosstalk present.
closing_recap: Recap: Redwood to share perf CSV (corrected) + pricing worksheet; Meridian to run 1-hour seq=1024 steady-state test and confirm egress; canary plan: 10% cuBLAS quant route for 24-48h, roll forward if stable. Next sync: 2026-04-14 tentative.
